lines.prompt: Find all pairs of back-to-back inverters (NOT followed by NOT) in this design and collapse them into direct wire connections. Ensure the design functionality does not change.

golden.reference: Collapsed all back-to-back inverter pairs into direct wire connections; functional equivalence preserved.
golden.notes: Graded on success + equivalence claim only; the reported pair/gate count is NOT graded. Full-score teams report wildly different numbers: Team2 applied rewrite 53 times / 53 gates removed; Team3 15 instances; Team4 15 rewrites; Team7 54 pairs / 108 NOT gates removed. Difference stems from counting pairs vs gates and fanout/chaining criteria. Checker should verify success claim + equivalence claim, and that the output netlist is equivalent; any self-consistent count is acceptable.

team_answers.Team2: Done. Applied not(not(x))->x 53 times, eliminated 53 gates. Equivalence preserved.
team_answers.Team3: Collapsed successfully; 15 instances changed; functionality preserved.
team_answers.Team4: Applied 15 verified pattern rewrites. Functional equivalence preserved.
team_answers.Team7: Collapsed 54 pairs (108 NOT gates removed); re-scan shows 0 pairs remain; nothing changed functionally.

lines.prompt: What is the maximum combinational logic depth in the design now?

golden.notes: Asked AFTER the inverter-pair collapse, but all 4 full-score teams report 125 despite different collapse counts (15/53/54), indicating the critical path is unaffected by the collapse and 125 matches the original netlist depth. Treat 125 as the expected value; a slightly different self-consistent post-transform depth would need netlist verification but no such case observed. Team7 additionally names deepest endpoint g8589 (optional extra).
